analysis.explanation: The Random Forest assigns a 0.93 malware probability, and all 20 top n-grams push toward cryptojacking. SHAP contributions are tightly clustered (+0.0055 to +0.0086), so no single feature dominates. The prediction rests on the combined pattern. The strongest theme is rotate and carry-chain arithmetic. MOV ROL (+0.008300, freq 0.001317), ADD ROR (+0.008303), MOVZX ROL (+0.006766), ROL ROR (+0.006750) and XOR ROL (+0.005918) show frequent rotation mixed with XOR and add operations. This is typical of hash and cipher round functions such as those in proof-of-work mining. Multi-precision arithmetic is suggested by SUB SBB (+0.006719), MOV ADC (+0.005977), SUB ADC (+0.005655) and ADC SUB (+0.005568). This is characteristic of big-number or wide-word computation. Stack-heavy and register-shuffling sequences (MOVZX PUSH, CALL PUSH, SUB PUSH, XOR PUSH, CMP PUSH, POP XOR, ADD POP) may reflect unrolled or inlined compute routines with heavy register save and restore. Rarer items such as CDQ MOV, MOVSX BTS and CMOVZ MOV add to the unusual instruction mix. The evidence includes no function names, API calls or strings, and each n-gram has a low frequency. Individual n-grams are therefore not conclusive, since rotates and add-with-carry also appear in legitimate crypto libraries and compression code. Even so, the consistent direction of all 20 features, the concentration of rotate/XOR/carry patterns, and the high model probability support a high-confidence call, with some caution because the evidence is purely statistical.

evidence_analysis.assessment: Top-ranked feature. Zero-extending a byte or word and pushing it is consistent with byte-oriented data handling before a hashing or cipher routine, but it is generic on its own.
Sign-extension followed by a move suggests signed 32-bit arithmetic. It is rare (freq 0.000188) but gets a high SHAP weight, so it is a model-specific marker rather than a clear mining behavior.
An add followed by a right rotate is a classic ARX (add-rotate-xor) building block in hash functions and ciphers used in proof-of-work.
Frequent (0.001317) load-then-rotate pattern consistent with hash round operations, which supports compute-intensive mining-style code.
Restoring a register then XORing it fits mixing steps in cryptographic routines, though it can also be a compiler idiom.
Call followed by a push shows function-boundary and stack setup. It is weakly informative alone and may indicate modular compute helper routines.
Arithmetic followed by a stack push, consistent with register spilling in dense arithmetic code. Contributes only as part of the overall pattern.
Zero-extended byte or word data feeding a rotate suggests byte-wise input being mixed in hash or cipher rounds.
Adjacent opposite rotations are uncommon in ordinary code and are associated with hash and cipher implementations, so this is a notable crypto-primitive indicator.
Subtract with borrow indicates multi-word arithmetic, as in big-integer or wide-word math sometimes used in mining algorithms.
Stack-epilogue or restore pattern. Low specificity, but it adds to the compute-routine signature.
Sign-extended load followed by a bit-test-and-set is an unusual combination that suggests bit manipulation. It is rare but weighted toward malware.
XOR followed by a push may indicate mixing or zeroing before a call. Moderately consistent with obfuscation or cipher setup.

Most frequent n-gram (0.023146). Consecutive increments suggest tight pointer or counter loops over data buffers, which is consistent with repetitive compute loops, though it is common in benign code.
Add-with-carry after a move indicates carry-chain arithmetic, supporting multi-precision or hash-style computation.
XOR with rotate is a core ARX pattern in hash and cipher rounds, a strong thematic match for mining primitives.
Comparison followed by a push is a control-flow and stack pattern with low specificity. It adds modest support.
Subtract followed by add-with-carry again points to extended-precision arithmetic, at a relatively high frequency of 0.002446.
The reverse carry/subtract ordering reinforces the multi-word arithmetic theme across the binary.
Conditional-move pattern with essentially zero frequency. It may reflect branchless selection logic, but its presence is marginal and the contribution is mainly model-driven.

key_indicators: Dense rotate/XOR/add (ARX-style) n-grams: MOV ROL, ADD ROR, ROL ROR, XOR ROL, MOVZX ROL
Carry/borrow arithmetic chains: SUB SBB, MOV ADC, SUB ADC, ADC SUB
All 20 top SHAP features push toward cryptojacking with consistent magnitudes
Tight-loop counter pattern INC INC at relatively high frequency (0.023146)
analysis.recommended_action: Treat as likely cryptojacking and prioritize for deeper analysis. Disassemble the functions containing the rotate/XOR and ADC/SBB sequences and check for known hash algorithm constants such as those of CryptoNight or RandomX. Then look for mining pool or network indicators and persistence behavior. Run the sample in a sandbox and monitor CPU utilization and outbound connections. Compare against legitimate crypto or compression libraries to rule out false positives.
